subject: Feature concession & roadmap alignment for Hearthside enterprise activation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hearthside: critical export + retention ask — need roadmap clarity

Team — quick context and ask: Hearthside (PROSPECT -> fast moving enterprise) verbally committed to a Q1 activation if we can bridge two gaps in our hosted product: 1) per-tenant audit/export streams that include full token-level metadata, and 2) 13-month export retention with S3-compatible delivery and configurable redaction rules. They flagged these as non-negotiable in procurement and will pause legal if we can’t provide an acceptable plan.

Why I’m looping you: Laura — need an ask on product commitment / can we fit a constrained MVP in the Q4 engineering slot? Priyom — can CS/solutions own a temporary shim (managed export + manual redaction process) for launch if engineering needs more runway? Irene — we need a rough engineering effort estimate and what API surface would look like (stream vs bulk, auth model).

Attached a compact heatmap showing the customer-impacted flows (MVP-scope-heatmap.pdf). High-level ask from me: can we produce a scoped plan (MVP definition, trade-offs, and timeline) by EOD Thursday so I can get Procurement a committed plan to avoid losing the close?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
---
(attachment: MVP-scope-heatmap.pdf (pdf))

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com, irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hearthside: critical export + retention ask — need roadmap clarity

Jordan — thanks for the heads-up and the heatmap. Quick thinking notes:

- Product perspective: This is aligned with an existing epics backlog around "tenant-specific telemetry exports" but current scope assumes 90-day export retention and a single export stream per org. Extending to 13 months and adding per-tenant redaction will increase storage and compliance surface area.

- MVP proposal (constrained): 1) Offer a streamed export webhook that delivers event batches (no token-level de-embedding in MVP) + 90-day retention on platform; 2) Provide an S3-handoff pipeline we can schedule nightly for longer retention (13 months) but with manual redaction controls via CS for first 3 months; 3) Commit to a Q2 roadmap item to add native 13-month retention and automated redaction.

Trade-offs: quicker time-to-close vs. additional manual work for CS and temporary caveats on automated redaction. If they require SLA-backed native retention from day one, that’s a heavier lift (capacity, billing model, KMS considerations).

Irene — can you give an estimate for the constrained MVP above? Priyom — if CS runs the manual redaction/S3-fanout, what operational burden is that for the team?

-Laura
Laura Bennett
VP Product, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 15:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hearthside: critical export + retention ask — need roadmap clarity

Laura / Jordan / Priyom — quick feasibility and rough effort estimate for the constrained MVP:

Summary of approach I’d recommend for MVP (minimal infra changes):
1) Streamed export webhook (HTTP POST batches) — 2 sprints (4 weeks) to implement: auth via JWT tied to tenant id, basic batching, retry semantics.
2) Nightly S3 fanout job (platform -> customer S3) — 2-3 sprints (6 weeks) if we reuse our existing export pipeline. This gives the 13-month retention externally without immediate internal storage growth.
3) Manual redaction workflow (CS-run) — product work small (1 sprint) to add an admin UI and redact markers; operational playbook to be owned by CS.

Risk/notes:
- KMS/customer-managed keys to S3 will add legal/compliance work — estimate additional 1 sprint for key management docs and tests.
- If Hearthside requires token-level tokenization metadata in the stream (they said "full token-level metadata"), that’s another 2-3 sprints to plumb through the runtime and format serializers.

Rough total for MVP scoping path (without full token-level metadata): 5-8 sprints (~10-16 weeks) if we sequence work in parallel across infra and export teams. If we compress by prioritizing export webhook + S3 fanout, we could aim for an initial ship in ~8 weeks.

I can write a narrower acceptance criteria doc for the MVP tomorrow morning if that helps Jordan's procurement cadence.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Runtime Services
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, irene_choi@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice@hearthside.com>, Hearthside Procurement <procurement@hearthside.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hearthside: critical export + retention ask — need roadmap clarity

Thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround and the pragmatic MVP path. Jordan / summary for procurement and next steps below (copying Hearthside so we have shared context):

- Agreed constrained MVP: streamed export webhook + nightly S3 fanout to customer bucket (13-month retention externally) + CS manual redaction UI for initial 90 days of operations.
- Timeline: Target initial ship in ~8 weeks (tentative target: 2028-01-26 ship window), with product/eng commitment to add native 13-month retention and automated redaction in the next major release (target Q2).
- Open items for legal/procurement: KMS/customer-managed key handling, data residency clause tweaks, and SLAs for export delivery. Jordan to share contract redlines this afternoon.

Alice / Procurement — can you confirm whether the S3 handoff + 13-month external retention is acceptable as a contractual commitment for activation? If so, I’ll route the contract redline and ask legal to add the timeline bullets. If Hearthside requires native platform retention (without external S3 handoff) to close, we’ll need an escalation window.

Attachments: contract-redline-v2.docx (I will send separately via DocuSign link once legal signs off).

Appreciate the team's alignment — Priyom, I can own the CS playbook and initial redaction tasks; please advise if you’ll need additional headcount or a time-limited contractor.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachment: contract-redline-v2.docx)
